item.title: Episode 17: Inside the Criminal Investigations Program at the CRA
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: The Criminal Investigations Program at the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) plays a crucial role in protecting Canada’s tax base by investigating important cases of tax evasion and other tax crimes. Program employees have expertise in digital forensics, criminal intelligence, data analysis, and other skills to help investigate those who deliberately choose to not pay their taxes. They focus on investigations such as organized tax schemes, international tax evasion, money laundering, and tax fraud. On this episode, we talk to two CRA employees about the Program’s work, the investigation tools they use, and their work with other international tax administrations.

item.title: Economic diplomacy: Opening doors for Canadian SME
item.author: Global Affairs Canada
item.content:encoded:
Did you know that 97% of Canadian businesses that export goods are small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)?
SMEs are the backbone of our economy and help drive growth, but expanding into global markets can feel risky. That is where economic diplomacy makes a real difference.
In this video, High Commissioner Bill Blair and Consul General Joanne Lemay explain how Canada helps local businesses scale up.
Canada already has doors open to over 1.5 billion consumers worldwide through 15 free trade agreements. By negotiating new deals, like a potential Canada-Mercosur agreement, we help lower costs and reduce risks in high-growth markets, as in Brazil. When Canadian small businesses plug into global supply chains, they create good jobs right here at home.

item.content:encoded: In this episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we focus on inclusion in the workplace, examining the persistent barriers faced by underrepresented groups and the innovative approaches helping to build more equitable career pathways. Host Jeremy Strachan is joined by Golnaz Golnaraghi, founder of Accelerate Her Future, who shares insights from a recent Future Skills Centre study on the systemic challenges racialized and Indigenous women encounter in advancing to leadership roles, and what organizations can do to dismantle these barriers. We then hear from Agapi Gessesse, CEO of the Canadian Institute for Leadership Advancement and Research (CILAR), who explores how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies can be leveraged to create more inclusive labour market opportunities for Black youth. item.title: What does a diplomat actually do?
item.author: Global Affairs Canada
item.content:encoded:
What is Economic Diplomacy?
It is much more than formal meetings. Today, economic diplomacy is about showing up where it matters most to deliver real results for people in both our nations.
Our team in London works every day to build strong partnerships and investments between Canada and the United Kingdom. They connect clean energy firms, technology leaders and innovators across both countries.
British direct investments support over 170,000 jobs in Canada. At the same time, Canadian direct investments support 190,000 jobs in the United Kingdom.
Why does this matter right now?
With the United Kingdom joining the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership trade deal, our shared partnership opens new doors across a $5.6-trillion global market. Lower tariffs and clearer rules make it easier for businesses in both countries to expand, lower costs and reduce risks.
When we build reliable partnerships abroad, we strengthen supply chains, boost economic security and create good jobs at home.

item.title: Retail Grocery in Canada: Our 3-Year Review
item.author: Competition Bureau Canada
item.content:encoded:
Food affordability remains a major concern for Canadians. While many global and economic factors affect food prices, competition plays an important role in keeping prices in check and supporting choice and innovation.
In this video, the Competition Bureau highlights the steps governments across Canada have taken since the publication of our 2023 retail grocery market study report. While progress has been made, we continue to encourage governments across Canada to implement the recommendations of our report.
Learn more about the follow-up and our recommendations:
https://competition-bureau.canada.ca/en/how-we-foster-competition/education-and-outreach/publications/assessing-progress-competition-bureaus-retail-grocery-recommendations?utm_campaign=cb-bc-social-media-26-27&utm_medium=smo&utm_source=yt&utm_content=grocery-en-260903

item.title: IP insurance: Can startups afford to defend their IP?
item.author: Lisa Desjardins (CIPO), Michael Huynh (IPON), Shanon Shanon (Navacord)
item.content:encoded: How can startups and SMEs protect the value of their IP when litigation costs can be overwhelming? Joining us for this episode are Michael Huynh, General Counsel at Intellectual Property Ontario, and Shannon Shannon, a commercial insurance broker at Navacord, to explore how IP insurance can help businesses defend and enforce their IP rights. They discuss what is covered by IP insurance, how premiums are calculated and how this emerging tool may help innovators manage risk, attract investment and commercialize their ideas with greater confidence.

item.title: Canada is helping create a healthier, stronger world for everyone
item.author: Global Affairs Canada
item.content:encoded:
Malnutrition doesn’t happen overnight... and it is not a choice.
When nutritious food becomes hard to get, women and children are often the most affected.
That’s why Canada is investing in something bigger: prevention.
Global hunger and nutrition are not distant issues, they are shared challenges with shared impacts.
Canada’s nutrition support in emergencies and investments in long term nutrition don’t just help communities abroad, they help build a more stable, secure, and prosperous world that also benefits people in Canada.

item.title: S6 Ep. 05 (Bonus): Supporting Indigenous Community Health Workers: Lessons from Ontario and Alaska
item.content:encoded: In this bonus episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we explore the critical role Indigenous community health workers play in supporting health and well-being in rural, remote, and northern communities. Guest host Bethany Haalboom is joined by Janet Gordon and Madison Pierce of the Sioux Lookout First Nations Health Authority, along with Dr. Michelle Hensel of the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium, to discuss how community-based health workers help bridge gaps in care, provide culturally grounded support, and strengthen healthcare access where providers and services are often limited. Drawing on experiences from Northwestern Ontario and Alaska, the conversation highlights innovative approaches to training, recruitment, retention, and workforce development, while underscoring the importance of investing in Indigenous-led solutions to improve health outcomes and build community capacity.Janet Gordon, Vice President of Community Health, Sioux Lookout First Nation Health AuthorityMadison Pierce, Manager of the Community Health Workers Diabetes Program, Sioux Lookout First Nation Health AuthorityDr. Michelle Hensel, Medical Director, Community Health Aide Program, Alaska Native Tribal Health ConsortiumJeremy Strachan, Manager, Education & Skills, Signal49 ResearchBethany Haalboom, Lead Research Associate, Indigenous and Northern Communities, Signal49 ResearchIndigenous Community Health Workers Across Canada (Project Website) English | FrenchTraining to Retain: Strengthening the Role of Indigenous Community Health Workers in Canada (Report) English | FrenchSpotlight: Sioux Lookout First Nations Diabetes ProgramEnglish | French

item.title: Framing the Next Policy Framework
item.author: Agriculture and Agri-food Canada
item.content:encoded: "In my mind, those frameworks are both an art and a science." That's how Dori Gingera-Beauchemin describes the work of building Canada's national agricultural frameworks. And right now, the next one is taking shape. The Next Policy Framework will run 2028 to 2033 and succeeds the Sustainable CAP. We speak with two people who have shaped these frameworks from every angle. Dori Gingera-Beauchemin spent forty-four years with the Manitoba Department of Agriculture, including a decade as Deputy Minister. She has sat at the table for every framework negotiation since the year 2000. Tyler McCann, managing director of the Canadian Agri-Food Policy Institute, has worked every side of the policy process from inside government, in industry, and on his own farm. Hear how policy moves the needle, where the next framework needs to focus, and why, as Tyler puts it, "we need to speak with one voice where we agree, and have respectful disagreement when we don't."

item.title: Challenging Exile: Japanese Canadians and the Wartime Constitution
item.author: Discover Library and Archives Canada
item.content:encoded: In September 1945, thousands of Japanese Canadians who had already endured internment and dispossession faced a new threat: forced exile to war-torn Japan. Join us for a thought-provoking conversation with Eric M. Adams and Jordan Stanger-Ross, authors of Challenging Exile: Japanese Canadians and the Wartime Constitution, moderated by Professor Emerita Audrey Kobayashi.

item.title: 🎭💙 Le Pays de la Sagouine – Bouctouche, New Brunswick
item.author: ACOACanada
item.content:encoded:
Experience the history of the Acadian culture at Le Pays de la Sagouine, a New Brunswick destination where the culture comes into live through music, theatre and immersive experiences.
ACOA is proud to support projects that help preserve and showcase our region’s rich culture. Through upgrades to its infrastructure, Le Pays de la Sagouine will enhance sustainability, improve their tourism experience, and continue sharing Acadian stories with visitors from near and far. 🎭
#GC
Transcription Every year, close to 100,000 thousand visitors experience the magic of Le Pays de la Sagouine.
With ACOA’s support, Le Pays de la Sagouine was able to sound proof a portion of the Viola-Léger Restaurant-Theatre, improve their welcome building by adding solar panels, and make the washrooms at Akadi Lumina accessible.
ACOA also helped with the marketing and promotion for Akadi Lumina, which just welcomed their 140,000th visitor.
Thanks to ACOA's funding, Le Pays de la Sagouine is able to continue to improve the client experience and to work towards our vision for the future.

item.title: Signaux de fumée : Comment la qualité de l'air extérieur nuit à la sécurité au travail
item.content:encoded: Les épisodes de mauvaise qualité de l'air sont en hausse, ce qui nuit à la santé et à la sécurité des personnes travaillant à l'extérieur et à l'intérieur. Avoir un plan clair avant que la fumée ou la poussière ne se répande n'est qu'une des choses que les employeurs peuvent faire pour maintenir les travailleurs en santé. Matea Kokorovic, spécialiste technique principale, se joint à nous pour discuter de ce que les employeurs et les travailleurs doivent savoir.

item.title: Smoke Signals: How Outdoor Air Quality Affects Workplace Safety
item.content:encoded: Poor air quality events are on the rise, affecting the health and safety of both outdoor and indoor workers. Having a clear plan ready before the smoke or dust rolls in is just one of the things employers can do to keep workers healthy. Senior Technical Specialist Matea Kokorovic joins us to discuss what employers and workers need to know.

item.title: A Honeybee Trivia Showdown
item.author: Statistics Canada
item.content:encoded: Think your honeybee knowledge is as sweet as honey? Time to put it to the test!In this special episode of Eh Sayers, our colleagues face off in a trivia showdown all about Canada’s honeybee industry and the tiny pollinators that play a huge role in our food system.Discover how much honey was produced, how many beekeepers are caring for colonies across the country, the surprising value of honey sales, and why bees are essential far beyond the honey they produce.After listening, you’ll be the go-to expert on honeybees at your next backyard gathering!

item.title: S6 Ep. 04: Building Canada’s AI Advantage
item.content:encoded: In this episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we explore what it will take for Canada to build and sustain a competitive edge in artificial intelligence. Host Jeremy Strachan speaks with three experts who each bring a different perspective on the opportunities and risks shaping Canada’s AI future. We begin with Aaron Rodericks, Head of Trust and Security at Bluesky, who offers a candid assessment of the global AI race—highlighting Canada’s position relative to major players, the realities of market concentration, and the emerging cybersecurity risks tied to rapidly advancing models. Next, Jaxson Khan, Senior Fellow at the Munk School of Global Affairs joins the podcast to unpack the concept of AI sovereignty, outlining what it means in practice across the AI stack and what structural and cultural shifts are needed for Canada to build, adopt, and retain AI capacity. Finally, CIFAR AI Chair at the University of Alberta Blair Attard-Frost reflects on Canada’s newly released AI strategy, emphasizing the importance of public trust, social research, and a broader cultural shift in how we approach innovation, governance, and talent retention. Together, this conversation explores what it will take not only to compete in the global AI landscape—but to do so in a way that is secure, sovereign, and socially grounded. Aaron Rodericks, Head of Trust and Security, Bluesky Jaxson Khan, Senior Fellow, Munk School of Global Affairs Blair Attard-Frost, CIFAR AI Chair and Assistant Professor, University of Alberta Jeremy Strachan, Manager, Education & Skills, Signal49 Research Conference Board of Canada, The. Ottawa: Government of Canada. English | FrenchMullen, Sean, and Jaxson Khan. Sovereign By Design: Strategic Options for Canadian AI Sovereignty. item.title: Atlantic Canada’s Aerospace & Defence Capabilities: Building a Stronger Future
item.author: ACOACanada
item.content:encoded:
Atlantic Canada is ready.
Ready to innovate. Ready to collaborate. Ready to help deliver the largest investment in Canadian defence and security in a generation.
The opportunities are here—and so are the people, expertise, and industry to make them happen. 👉 https://ow.ly/v1j250Zp4qc
Transcript The world is changing rapidly. Less certain, less stable. That's why Canada has launched its first defence industrial strategy. To protect our sovereignty, security and prosperity while supporting Canadian workers innovation and long term economic growth. The strategy puts Canadian builders first, creating jobs and greater stability. ACOA is supporting Atlantic Canadian businesses through advocacy and action with programs like the Regional Defence Investment Initiative. Turning regional strength into global opportunity. Companies across Atlantic Canada are scaling up, creating jobs, expanding capacity, advancing innovation and delivering for Canada and our allies. From engineering and advanced manufacturing to skilled trades and digital innovation, ACOA investments are helping people and communities. Serious investments at home. A stronger defence sector. Keeping Canada and our allies safe.

item.title: Episode 14: Understanding the Collections Process
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: The collections process happens when you owe the CRA money. This may sound overwhelming at first, but we’re here to help you understand it. You could be in the collections process for several reasons, like life changes that affect your financial situation or a small tax-filing error. Our guest is here to guide us through the process. They’ll give you tips on how to take proactive steps to pay your debts with the CRA and how to work with a collections officer to resolve them. Even if you or a family member don’t owe the CRA money, this episode is still a great opportunity to understand how the process works.

item.title: What Occupational Health and Safety Could Look Like in 2040
item.content:encoded: Dr. Arif Jetha recently led a research study that scanned nearly 400 signals of change to map out where occupational health and safety is headed. He explains why leaders need to balance today's challenges with tomorrow's, and what employers, policymakers and workers can do to stay ahead.

item.title: S6 Ep. 03: The Care Economy
item.content:encoded: In this episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we turn to the care economy—one of Canada's most essential yet complex labour market sectors. Host Jeremy Strachan is joined by Anita Khanna, Vice President of Government Relations and Public Policy at United Way Centraide, who explains why care work—from long-term care to community services—operates differently from other sectors, facing persistent challenges with worker retention, job quality, and wage disparities. We then hear from Tyler Downey, President of SEIU Healthcare, who outlines how unions are helping to build pathways into the care economy—particularly through targeted training and supports that enable internationally educated nurses to enter and thrive in Canada's healthcare workforce. We close with Sean Chilton, CEO of Health Workforce Canada, who highlights the critical role of high-quality, integrated data in understanding workforce gaps, improving planning, and driving better health workforce outcomes across the country. Together, this conversation explores what it will take to stabilize, strengthen, and grow the care workforce at a time of rising demand and system-wide pressure.Anita Khanna, Vice President, Government Relations and Public Policy, United Way CentraideSean Chilton, President and CEO, Health Workforce CanadaTyler Downey, President, SEIU HealthcareJeremy Strachan, Manager, Education & Skills, Signal49 ResearchAnnouncement of United Way Centraide Canada's National Labour Force Strategy: English | FrenchHealth Workforce Canada's Pan-Canadian Health Workforce Data Strategy: EnglishFrenchPathways for International Educated Health Care Professionals (Insights Report):English | French

item.title: Orange Skies, Smoky Air and Billions at Risk of Going Up in Smoke
item.author: Statistics Canada
item.content:encoded: Orange skies, record breaking fire seasons, and smoke that travels thousands of kilometres have made wildfires impossible to ignore. But beyond the visible destruction lies another story, one measured not only in burned forests and evacuations, but also in economic impacts that ripple across communities and industries.How do wildfires affect Canada's economy? How are these impacts measured? And what do they tell us about the challenges Canadians may face in the years ahead?In this episode, we spoke with Mike Flannigan, a leading expert on wildfire science and climate change at Thompson Rivers University, and Mark Brown, Principal Researcher at Statistics Canada, to explore how wildfires are reshaping Canada’s forests, communities, and economy.

item.title: Episode 13: Crypto and taxes – All the facets to crypto-assets
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: On this episode, we’re diving into the ever-evolving, blockchain-powered world of crypto-assets! The crypto space can be exciting, but also unpredictable and sometimes a little confusing. Even so, crypto-asset activities do have an impact on your taxes. So we’re here to make sure you don’t get lost on the blockchain when tax time approaches. If you have a basic understanding of crypto, are looking to get into it, or already own crypto-assets and want to know its impact on your taxes, this episode is for you

item.title: Testing business ideas: Aligning strategy with IP protection
item.author: Lisa Desjardins (CIPO), David Bland (Author), Kevin Dahl (Innovate Calgary)
item.content:encoded: David Bland, author of , and Kevin Dahl, Director of ElevateIP Alberta at Innovate Calgary, explore how to better balance your business strategy with IP considerations. Consider gathering real evidence from customers before spending a fortune building the wrong product. Learn how to identify your riskiest business assumptions using practical frameworks and strategically structure your testing process to avoid accidentally disclosing or compromising your valuable IP.

item.title: The Evolution of Psychological Health and Safety
item.content:encoded: In today's workplace, we know that prioritizing psychological safety alongside physical safety is part of building a truly healthy and safe environment. But that hasn't always been the case. Consultant and expert Mary Ann Baynton joins us to discuss how approaches to psychological health and safety have evolved over time.

item.title: Howie Morenz: Hockey's First Legend
item.author: Discover Library and Archives Canada
item.content:encoded: In this episode, we feature a discussion between Andrew Ross, Director, Research Support at Library and Archives Canada and Donald Murray, author of Howie Morenz: The Greatest Season in the Life of Hockey’s First Legend. Join us as we unravel what made Howie Morenz one of hockey’s most compelling figures, on and off the ice.

item.title: S6 Ep. 02: A Workforce to Build Big
item.content:encoded: In this episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we focus on Canada’s big build moment—when major infrastructure, industrial expansion, and nation‑building projects are converging with profound workforce pressures. Host Jeremy Strachan is joined by former Ontario Minister of Labour and Infrastructure Monte McNaughton to explore why apprenticeships, early pathways into the skilled trades, and labour mobility are essential as retirements accelerate and demand surges. We then hear from Mike Gordon, Director of Canadian Training of the United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters, who unpacks why training quality, credential recognition, and national standards are critical to mobilizing a skilled workforce—without taking risky shortcuts. We close with Pari Johnston, President and CEO of Colleges and Institutes Canada, who makes the case for public colleges as the backbone of Canada’s skills ecosystem, and what it will take to deliver training at the speed, scale, and quality needed to prepare workers for an AI‑driven economy. Monte McNaughton, Co-Chair, Future Skills Centre Resilient Workforce Working Table Mike Gordon, Director of Canadian Training, United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters Pari Johnston, President and CEO, Colleges and Institutes Canada

item.title: Managing IP disputes: mediation, arbitration and other solutions
item.author: Lisa Desjardins (CIPO), Justine Ferland (WIPO), Gary Lacasse (ADRIC)
item.content:encoded: Facing an IP dispute? There are resolution options that don’t require going to court and the associated fees. Gary Lacasse, Executive Director of the Alternative Dispute Resolution Institute of Canada (ADRIC) and Justine Ferland, legal officer, WIPO Arbitration and Mediation Centre, explore how alternative dispute resolution can help resolve conflicts and protect intellectual property. From mediation to arbitration, they discuss when these approaches make sense and how they help preserve time and business relationships.

item.title: The Grey Anatomy of Canada: The Story Behind Canada’s Aging Population
item.author: Statistics Canada
item.content:encoded: Canada’s population is getting a makeover, and it is changing the way we live. We are digging into new demographic data with Patrick Charbonneau, Section Chief in Demography at Statistics Canada, to see how big boomer and millennial generations, plus fewer younger people, are shaking up demand for housing, schools, and healthcare. We also look at the rise of the sandwich generation, the caregiving squeeze that comes with longer lives and smaller families, and the many ways older Canadians keep things running through volunteering, childcare, and family support.

item.title: Data-Driven Approaches to Health and Safety
item.content:encoded: Association of Workers' Compensation Boards of Canada CEO Janet MacEachern joins us to discuss national injury trends, and how workplaces can use AWCBC's data to support prevention locally.

item.title: S6 Ep. 01: A Future Built on Skills
item.content:encoded: In this episode of the Future Skills Podcast, we tee up the new season by diving into Canada’s hinge moment for talent, productivity, and resilience by revisiting some of the key themes from A Future Built on Skills. This one-day hybrid event from October 2025 brought together thought leaders in skills, training and workforce development. We’re joined by the Future Skills Centre’s Noel Baldwin in conversation with the Honourable Patty Hajdu, Minister of Jobs and Families, exploring an all‑hands‑on‑deck approach to workforce resilience—why soft skills, apprenticeships, and work‑integrated learning matter as major projects and trades demand surge. Then J.P. Giroux, President of the Excellence in Manufacturing Consortium, takes us onto the factory floor to unpack how automation and AI are reshaping roles, why SMEs must treat training as strategy, and how a culture of continuous learning drives real productivity gains. We close with Professor Wendy Cukier, Academic Director and Founder of the Diversity Institute at Toronto Metropolitan University, who makes the case for a national skills agenda centered on SMEs, inclusion (EDI), and scenario planning for AI, and what a blueprint for preparing Canada’s workforce for 2026 and beyond looks like.The Honourable Patty Hajdu, Minister of Jobs and Families, Government of CanadaNoel Baldwin, Executive Director, Future Skills CentreJ.P. Giroux, President, Excellence in Manufacturing ConsortiumWendy Cukier, Academic Director and Founder, Diversity Institute

item.title: From Idea to Adoption: Olds College smart farm
item.author: Agriculture and Agri-food Canada
item.content:encoded: Turning high-tech concepts into field-ready tools requires more than just a good idea—it requires real-world validation and farmer-to-farmer trust. In this episode, we speak with Herman Simons, who leads Smart Agriculture Applied Research at Olds College in Alberta. He oversees dozens of projects each year that test emerging technologies.. We’re also joined by agronomist, Steve Larocque, an independent crop advisor who works with producers and with Olds College to turn new ideas into practical, field-ready systems.The Canadian Intellectual Property Office’s new tool, IP Central, brings you all the IP support you need in one place, with clear guidance, how-to resources, and links to funding and events from trusted partners.

item.title: How the Innovation Asset Collective helps cleantech companies succeed
item.author: Lisa Desjardins (CIPO), Erin Pisko (IAC)
item.content:encoded: The Innovation Asset Collective (IAC) is on a mission to help cleantech companies understand the value of their IP. Erin Pisko, Vice-President of IP Strategy at the IAC, uses real-world examples to show on which components of an IP strategy cleantech companies should focus. The IAC’s core programming provides a comprehensive suite of supports, including funding and skill-building to help increase patenting activity in the cleantech sector.

item.title: Canada’s Happiness Crisis (And Why It’s Not All Doom and Gloom)
item.author: Statistics Canada
item.content:encoded: Everyone wants to be happy, but just how happy are Canadians? On this episode of the Eh Sayers podcast, join quality of life experts from Statistics Canada and Engage Nova Scotia to explore the importance of quality of life programs and what they tell us about our well-being.

item.title: Jour de deuil: L'histoire de Jessica Blackie Gillis
item.content:encoded: L'ambassadrice de Threads of Life, Jessica Blackie Gillis, a vu sa vie basculer le jour où son frère est décédé dans une tragédie évitable sur son lieu de travail. Écoutez son témoignage bouleversant.

item.title: Day of Mourning - Jessica Blackie Gillis' Story
item.content:encoded: Threads of Life Ambassador Jessica Blackie Gillis' life changed forever the day her brother died in a preventable workplace tragedy. Hear her powerful story.

item.title: Anne of Green Gables Chocolates - Charlottetown, PEI
item.author: ACOACanada
item.content:encoded:
Anne of Green Gables Chocolates credits its success to quality local ingredients, modern innovation, and a pinch of Anne Shirley’s creative charm. ACOA is proud to support the P.E.I business as they continue to grow.
Transcript 📍 Prince Edward Island ANNE OF GREEN GABLES CHOCOLATES The best stories begin in Avonlea! Anne of Green Gables Chocolates began handcrafting sweets there in 1999... ...and they’ve been adding new chapters ever since.
Their most famous innovation? Chocolate-covered potato chips, known whimsically as COW Chips
Modernized production lines have been key to meeting growing demand. Visitors can catch a glimpse of the action at the flagship Milky Way location!
Behind the scenes, inventory is managed efficiently through integrated data systems. Distributing decadent treats to 📍5 Island locations 📍major Canadian retail partners 📍 a booming online storefront!
So, what’s the recipe for success? ✅Local ingredients ✅Modern innovation ✅Uncompromised quality
ACOA is proud to support Anne of Green Gables Chocolates as they continue to grow!

item.title: Announcement for federal defence investment in Newfoundland and Labrador
item.author: ACOACanada
item.content:encoded:
Please note that simultaneous interpretation is not available for this livestream. A captioned recording and transcript in French will be made available following the event.
Veuillez noter que l’interprétation simultanée n’est pas offerte pour cette diffusion continue en direct. Un enregistrement et une transcription avec sous-titres français seront disponibles après l’évènement.

item.title: Inside Elevate IP - How Canadian startups can access funding, and IP expertise
item.author: Lisa Desjardins (CIPO), Laura Cooke (ISED), Louis-Félix Binette (MAIN), Lola Arnaud (MAIN)
item.content:encoded: How does ElevateIP help deliver IP support to businesses? Laura Cooke (ISED), Louis-Félix Binette, and Lola Arnaud (MAIN) answer this important question and more. Hear about how to access funding and how support is structured to promote long-term growth for your company.Note: This episode was recorded in 2023 and since then ElevateIP has been awarded new funding to continue delivering on their mission to help businesses build their IP strategies.

item.title: Episode 12: Tax tips for filing time!
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: On this episode, it’s about everyone’s favourite time of the year, tax season! Ok, that’s probably not true, but it is still an important time to determine if you are eligible for a refund, or any benefit or credit amounts to help you throughout the year. File your taxes on time and make sure they are accurate to receive the correct payment amounts, and avoid any delays. Our subject matter experts are here to help you prepare your 2025 income tax return. What you need to know: new changes this tax season ways to file or make changes to a return, and how to track the status of your return online.

item.title: Made with Local - Windsor, Nova Scotia
item.author: ACOACanada
item.content:encoded: Made With Local's CEO and Founder Sheena Russel is showing us how strong relationships and supporting local can make big impact. See how taking "support local" to heart has helped grow the business into a nationally recognized brand, and read the full story here: https://www.canada.ca/en/atlantic-canada-opportunities/campaigns/impacts/made-with-local.html

item.title: Navigating the global ocean of IP—A Black entrepreneur’s perspective on protection and opportunity
item.author: CIPO, Ken Poulin
item.content:encoded: Ken Poulin is an independent trademark agent based in Vancouver. He explains why IP protection should start before and not after market success. As a Black entrepreneur himself, he shares his insights on what it looks like to support underrepresented communities, the role of diversity in Canada's innovation landscape and why educating business owners about the value of IP requires patience, empathy and a personal approach.

item.title: Supporting Workers with Chronic Pain
item.content:encoded: Chronic pain affects 1 in 5 Canadians. It may occur after an injury has healed, or without a known cause. Dr. Andrea Furlan, a pain doctor from the University Health Network at the University of Toronto, joins us to discuss how employers can support workers affected by chronic pain, and how workers can find relief.

item.title: Episode 11: Helping small businesses across the country through the Liaison Officer service
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: Being a small business owner or self-employed individual is a lot of work - meeting clients, fulfilling online orders, developing your business’s website, and much more. If you’re acting as the accountant for your business, you also keep your business records up to date for taxes. Did you know the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) has a program to help you, for free? Through the CRA’s Liaison Officer service, you can get personalized support to help you understand your tax obligations. On this episode, a CRA liaison officer tells us all about the program. You’ll learn what’s involved in a typical meeting , what help an officer provides, and how to schedule your own personalized visit!

item.title: Women farmers leading into the future
item.author: Agriculture and Agri-food Canada

item.title: Bar U Ranch: Grass Into Money
item.content:encoded: For seven decades, the Bar U operated as a corporate ranch, with thousands of cattle fattening up on protein-rich fescue grass in Alberta’s Rocky Mountain foothills. But that grass has a history of its own, co-evolving on this landscape with a different grazer - the bison - over thousands of years. Through the history of three animals who’ve left their hoofmarks upon the prairie grasslands - bison, cattle and horses - we look at Canada’s “beef bonanza” that employed a colourful cast of cowboys, cooks and capitalists, turning grass into money at Bar U Ranch National Historic Site.Special thanks to Jessica Hill.Do you have a suggestion for a new National Historic Person, Site or Event? We’d love to hear it! Visit https://parks.canada.ca/commemorate for details on how to submit a nomination.

item.title: Waterton Lakes: Archaeology in a Burned Landscape
item.content:encoded: In August 2017, a lightning strike near Waterton Lakes National Park sparked a devastating wildfire that burned nearly 40% of the park. But in the wake of destruction came a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. We’ll hear from archaeologists and Blackfoot elders about the collaborative archaeology project that’s deepening our understanding of the lives of Indigenous peoples who have lived and travelled in the Rocky Mountains and foothills for millennia. Do you have a suggestion for a new National Historic Person, Site or Event? We’d love to hear it! Visit https://parks.canada.ca/commemorate for details on how to submit a nomination.

item.title: Special - Name Change
Fort Lennox: The Accidental Immigrants
item.content:encoded: In 1930s Europe, thousands of Jewish men and teenagers escaped the Nazi regime as refugees, only to be labelled as “enemy aliens” and sent to internment camps across eastern Canada. One of those camps was at Fort Lennox, an old military stronghold on Quebec’s Ile aux Noix. We’ll hear from one internee, the late Rabbi Erwin Schild, whose story helps illustrate the experience of hundreds of German and Austrian Jews who were imprisoned at Fort Lennox National Historic Site.Oral history recordings of Rabbi Erwin Schild used in this episode:Faye Blum of the Ontario Jewish Archives Teigan Goldsmith of the Ottawa Jewish Archives The Montreal Holocaust Museum The Toronto Holocaust Museum Do you have a suggestion for a new National Historic Person, Site or Event? We’d love to hear it!

item.title: Sit, Stand, Stretch: Preventing Repetitive Strain Injuries at Work
item.content:encoded: Whether work involves prolonged sitting or standing, reducing repetitive strain injuries starts with identifying the hazards and risk factors and improving job design. Here's where workplaces can start.

item.title: Red Bay: Discovering the Basque Whalers of Terra Nova
item.content:encoded: The southern coast of Labrador in the 1500s was the scene of Canada’s first oil boom. Each summer, Basque crews from Spain and France traversed the Atlantic to hunt whales and render their blubber into a precious commodity: oil that lit the lamps of Europe. It was dangerous, messy… and profitable. The story was all but lost until the 1970s, when researchers and archaeologists flocked to the tiny community of Red Bay, digging in the gardens and diving in the harbour, to uncover the secrets of Red Bay National Historic Site, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.Special thanks to Joxe Felipe Auzmendi and Iñaki Beraetxe, to Daniel Payne for use of his song and to Javier Vicente for recording assistance. Our condolences to the family of Robert Grenier, who led Parks Canada’s underwater archaeology work at Red Bay. Robert passed away in January 2026. Do you have a suggestion for a new National Historic Person, Site or Event? We’d love to hear it!

item.title: ReCollections is back for Season Two
item.content:encoded:
ReCollections, the award-winning history and archaeology podcast from Parks Canada, is back for Season Two. Four new stories from national parks and national historic sites across Canada:
Red Bay: Discovering the Basque Whalers of Terra Nova Fort Lennox: The Accidental Immigrants Bar U Ranch: Grass Into MoneyWaterton Lakes: Archaeology in a Burned Landscape Join us for a journey of national historic significance.

item.title: GDP Explained Without Putting You to Sleep (We Promise!)
item.author: Statistics Canada
item.content:encoded: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) tells us about the health and size of Canada’s economy. But for those of us who don’t own or operate multi-million-dollar companies, why does it matter at all? In this episode, Amanda Sinclair, Assistant director for the National Economic Accounts at Statistics Canada, explains some surprising ways GDP can be useful and why, for certain Canadian households, the numbers don’t always seem to add up.

item.title: Episode 10: Get help faster with the Canada Revenue Agency’s digital services
item.source: Taxology – The Official Canada Revenue Agency Podcast
item.content:encoded: Canadians expect and deserve reliable and timely service from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). We understand that not knowing where to find the information you need can be frustrating. That’s why we’re dedicated to enhancing our services and simplifying the process for you. On this episode, our expert guest helps you handle your common tax and benefit tasks online. We’ll cover digital services and tools to get help faster, and new improvements that make it easier to manage your whole tax situation. Listen to this episode to learn the fastest way to change your address with the CRA, check the status of a file, chat online with a CRA agent, and much more!
